title: First records with Sharkey in 1936
summary: Hug describes the personnel, tunes and difficult conditions of the Roosevelt Hotel session.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: No, my first records were with Shawkey Banana in 1936 when Shawkey Banana came with them. And we were playing together then. Where is the Shawpery? The Shawpery is now called Maison's Beach House out on Ponchacrine Boulevard. Were the records made in New Orleans? Oh, yes. I made the records with Shawkey at the Roosevelt Hotel. Who was in that band anyway? I think it was Ray Bonitas, Augie Chalang, Myer Wine Boyd, and I was in the band.
And then, I was in the band. Where is the Shawpery?
The Shawpery is now called Maison's Beach House out on Ponchacrine Boulevard.
Were the records made in New Orleans?
Oh, yes. I made the records with Shawkey at the Roosevelt Hotel.
Who was in that band anyway?
I think it was Ray Bonitas, Augie Chalang, Myer Wine Boyd, Julian Langan, Shawkey. I think that was about it.
What did Myer Wine Boyd play? Clarinet.
Of course, he goes in the name of Gene Myers now.
Clarinet. Did you have a saxophone playing?
Well, let's see, wait a minute.
I think we had two or three saxes, because Dave Weinstein also played sax. Now, I don't remember whether we had two saxes or three saxes on that section.
And what tunes did you cover?

We did Everybody Loves My Baby, Yes She Do, No She Don't. And then we recorded about six or eight other tunes that were never released. That was really a rough session, because we didn't have air conditioning in those days, and we were hot and bothered, and the piano was all out of tune, and we were recording in one room, and the recording equipment was in another room. It was all set up real bad, you know? We played so long that, of course, everybody's lips were getting bad, and Shawkey's lip was getting bad, and we were all getting...
